# Load required packages

# Introduction

Before using LundTax subtypes and signature scores downstream, it is worth checking that the
classifier had what it needed. `get_qc_report()` collects this information for a cohort:

- which samples could not be classified, and which calls are low confidence,
- how many of the genes used by the classifiers and signature scores were found in the data,
- whether any samples have an expression distribution that differs from the rest of the cohort.

`plot_qc_report()` shows the same information in one figure.

# Generate a QC report

Run the classifier with `include_data = TRUE`, so that the QC report can also check the
expression data:

```{r classify}
sjodahl_classes = classify_samples(this_data = sjodahl_2017,
                                   include_data = TRUE,
                                   verbose = FALSE)

sjodahl_qc = get_qc_report(these_predictions = sjodahl_classes)
```

Printing the report gives a short summary:

```{r print-qc}
sjodahl_qc
```

Per-sample details are in `$samples`, one row per sample:

```{r samples}
head(sjodahl_qc$samples[, c("sample_id", "subtype_5_class", "prediction_delta_collapsed",
                            "low_confidence", "missing_rules_5_class", "expr_median",
                            "distribution_outlier")])
```

which makes it easy to list the samples that need a second look:

```{r flagged}
subset(sjodahl_qc$samples, low_confidence | !classified | distribution_outlier,
       select = c(sample_id, subtype_5_class, prediction_delta_collapsed))
```

The report also contains `$signature_coverage`, `$classifier_coverage` and `$data_check` (the
log2 check). See `?get_qc_report` for all columns.

# Plot the QC report

```{r plot-qc, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 11}
plot_qc_report(these_qc = sjodahl_qc)
```

How to read the panels:

- **Prediction confidence**: the difference between the highest and second highest prediction
  score for each sample. Samples below the dashed line (`delta_threshold`, default 0.2) are
  flagged as low confidence (crosses).
- **Expression distribution per sample**: each point is one sample, showing its median expression
  against its interquartile range. Samples processed like the rest of the cohort form a tight
  cloud. Samples outside the dashed lines are flagged (red). A sample far to the left or right is
  shifted overall (e.g. not log2-transformed, or normalized separately); a sample far up or down
  has an unusual spread (e.g. many zeros).
- **Signature genes present** and **Classifier rules complete**: the share of the signature genes
  and classifier gene pairs found in the data.
- **Missing classifier rules per sample**: samples with at least one rule that could not be
  evaluated. Samples to the right of the dashed `impute_reject` line are not classified.

To save the figure, use `out_path` (and optionally `out_format`, `file_name`, `plot_width` and
`plot_height`):

```{r save-plot, eval = FALSE}
plot_qc_report(these_qc = sjodahl_qc, out_path = "qc/", out_format = "pdf")
```

# Adjusting the thresholds

The default cut-offs are heuristics for flagging samples worth a second look, not validated
thresholds. Both can be changed:

```{r thresholds}
strict_qc = get_qc_report(these_predictions = sjodahl_classes,
                          delta_threshold = 0.4,
                          outlier_mads = 2)

strict_qc$summary[, c("n_low_confidence", "n_distribution_outliers")]
```

# What to do with flagged samples

| Flag | What it means | Suggested action |
|---|---|---|
| Not classified | Too many classifier genes missing or NA | Check gene identifiers and missing values for the sample |
| Low confidence | Two subtypes score almost equally | Report the call with care, or look at the prediction scores |
| Distribution outlier | Sample processed or normalized differently | Subtype call is usually still fine (gene-pair rules); treat immune/stromal scores and heatmaps with caution |

If `classify_samples()` was run without `include_data = TRUE`, the expression data can be passed
to `get_qc_report()` with `this_data`. Without any expression data, the report still covers
prediction confidence, unclassified samples and signature coverage.
